chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Buhlul ibn Muslim, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever dies within less than fourteen days (of illness), his death would have been a sudden death.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْماً: Fourteen days — the prescribed threshold period; dying within this period of illness counts as sudden death.
key_terms.مَوْتَ فَجْأَةٍ: Sudden death (mawt faj'a) — death without adequate prior warning or illness period. Has specific legal implications in Islamic jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of sudden death in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the threshold for a death to be classified as 'sudden': if a person dies within less than fourteen days from the onset of illness, it is considered mawt faj'a (sudden death). This ruling has jurisprudential significance in Shia fiqh, particularly concerning whether the person had sufficient time to settle debts, make bequests, and perform religious obligations before dying. The fourteen-day threshold distinguishes a genuinely sudden death from one preceded by a warning period of illness that allowed the person to prepare.
